# Intent, direction, user-experience, and scope lens

Assess the proposal as a product and workflow change using high-effort
judgment. Read the whole user journey and the relevant trusted project
direction before producing candidates. Reconstruct the current proposal from
the issue plus the latest substantive maintainer clarifications in the
conversation. When a maintainer explicitly corrects the original direction,
assess the corrected direction and do not repeat the superseded concern.

## Intent and problem clarity

Determine whether the issue names a concrete user or project problem, affected
people, desired outcome, and observable success conditions. Separate the intent
from a prematurely chosen implementation.

## Direction

AI-DLC is a workflow, a framework, and a software factory. A person starts with
one intent; the workflow derives an explicit scope and carries it through the
stages, decisions, artifacts, implementation, validation, and operations needed
to deliver verified software. One hand-authored methodology is projected across
supported harnesses. Evaluate whether the proposal strengthens that
intent-to-scope-to-software chain, preserves lifecycle traceability and user
control, and avoids fragmenting the methodology.

## User Experience

Trace what changes before, during, and after the workflow:

- commands, parameters, configuration, defaults, migration, and discoverability;
- questions, approvals, gates, retries, stages, agents, model calls, latency,
  and token cost;
- feedback, interruption, recovery, failure states, and harness parity;
- the mandatory working relationship: in every user-facing interaction, the
  orchestrator speaks as a colleague helping build the user's software. It
  must not present itself as a model, bot, robot, or impersonal workflow.

## Scope and outcomes

Determine whether the scope is coherent, bounded, testable, and small enough to
plan. Identify essential boundaries, artifacts, outcomes, or acceptance
criteria missing from the issue. Do not demand arbitrary non-goals.

Use product taste to remove accidental complexity and expose confusing user
journeys, but do not turn personal wording preference into a finding. Write
concise candidate findings for the final judge. End with exactly the completion
marker provided after this prompt.
